newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cullen suspects NZ First resourcing deal.
newsitem.headline: Cullen suspects NZ First resourcing deal.

text.p: Labour deputy leader Michael Cullen said on Thursday he believed an "off the record" deal had been struck between National and NZ First over resourcing NZ First.
But Justice Minister Doug Graham said he was not aware of any such arrangement.

On Wednesday, NZ First and the conservative National Party signed a coalition deal after eight weeks of negotiations. NZ First held the balance of power after the October 12 election and negotiated separately with both Labour and National before opting for National on Tuesday.
Cullen said the non-policy parts of the deal were very similar to the one handed to Labour and drafted by NZ First leader Winston Peters' brother Wayne.
"This agreement has scarcely been changed from the original draft. Except one large interesting section that has been dropped out completely (covering) resourcing of NZ First," Cullen told Reuters.
"And I think that is an off-record deal now. I think it has been taken out to avoid embarrassment. There is a massive off record deal there which we could never match."
Cullen said he would not say what it involved "but I might in the House tomorrow".

Justice Minister Doug Graham, who was a key negotiator of the agreement, refused to discuss whether funding for NZ First arose during the negotiations. He said there were no arrangements "off balance sheet" that he was aware of.
"Not what you are getting at. Nothing of importance. Understandings of the kind I think you are referring to. No, there are none. Unless the prime minister has done it off his own bat," Graham said.
Cullen also said he was convinced nationalist New Zealand First's caucus did not get a true account of Labour's offer before making its choice of a coalition partner.
"I think Winston made up his mind before he went in there. I don't think the others did.
"I am now absolutely convinced that our position on a number of key issues was misrepresented in the last stages of their caucus," Cullen said.
Cullen said NZ First came back to Labour on Tuesday with a final offer of four seats in the cabinet when Labour had already offered six. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
